description:
An extern analysed on an input row where every contract clause is Underconstrained or Invalid publishes no return evidence. The settled return then reads as none, and the extern's native body lowers to 'trap user1'; the caller still expects a value, so the program dies with an illegal instruction instead of a compile-time diagnostic.

The path (develop c16ecee47):
1. src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:329-340, the extern's contract loop in AnalyzeActivation. activation_contract_return (:2033) returns applied.result; FunctionContract::apply (src/compiler2/contract.rs ~196-252) sets result only on a Known clause. Underconstrained (contract.rs:220; arrow_match.rs:349 and :367) and Invalid contribute nothing.
2. An extern runs no body walk, so return_evidence (semantic.rs ~292) stays None and define_activation_return publishes that (:379).
3. The settled return is read as types.none() (src/compiler2/semantic.rs:105, :131); lower_extern_executable (src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs:694, :716) passes it as the body's return type.
4. driver.rs:832 sets return_diverges = is_empty(return_ty); emit_return_term emits trap user1 (native_codegen/terminator.rs:516).

Invalid on an any argument is silent too: externs are always enforced (semantic.rs ~2010) but spec_violation_is_actionable (:2026) is false when an argument is any or has vars.

Reachability: not reached on develop. Eleven programs (dbg over closures, tuples and lists of closures, captures, send, make_resource with any arguments) ran correctly on interp, run and build; two with any arguments violating a typed extern panic at run time with 'extern integer arg must be Int' on all paths (loud, at the extern boundary). It was reached only under the #302 Gate B spike, which bound dbg(t) :: t to a tuple holding a closure and left the result Underconstrained. Not proven unreachable from the code: nothing at settle strips type variables from activation inputs.

Wanted: an extern whose SETTLED return evidence is None is a compile error naming the extern and the contract applied to the settled input row, reported through emit_through / Diagnostic::error as emit_spec_violation does (semantic.rs:2051). The check sits where the settled evidence is in hand: project_executable_facts (src/compiler2/executable_facts.rs ~261) or lower_extern_executable. It tests 'settled evidence is None', not is_empty: a contract that is Known(none) is legitimate and still traps. Mid-climb None is the legitimate bottom and is not an error.

Blocked on a failing test: no source program constructs the row. The test needs a way to produce an Underconstrained extern row through the production path.
title: An extern whose contract publishes no result is a loud error, not a trap body
